newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand limits foreign banks' offshore loans.
newsitem.headline: Thailand limits foreign banks' offshore loans.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said on Monday it set limits on offshore loans that foreign banks' offshore banking units under Bangkok International Banking Facility (BIBF) bring in for relending to local borrowers.

The central bank spokeswoman said the ratio of out-in loans to local baht-denominated loans granted by the offshore BIBF units of existing foreign banks' branches during September-December would be limited at the ratio of 1 to 1.
Currently there is no set ratio.
There are now 10 BIBF foreign bank branches.

Out-in loans refer to foreign funds that offshore banks import for relending to local clients. Out-out loans are foreign funds brought in for processing by Thai-based banks which relend them to borrowers in third countries.
The BOT last Friday issued the similar limits on out-in loans of offshore bankings units of Thai commercial banks.

She said any out-in loan increase above the required ratio would be permitted only if offshore banking units of foreign banks branches extended addtional out-out loans on a respective ratio of five to one during the same period.
The BOT also limited the out-in loans of BIBF units of foreign banks' representative offices to a maximum of only 5.6 percent of their out-in loans in August, she said.
There are currrently 19 BIBF foreign bank representative offices in Thailand.
